mainText: Good morning, Landon. Here's your brief for Wednesday, November 18, 2026. Stocks fell on Tuesday. The Dow dropped about 849 points, or 1.6 percent, to 50,759. The S&P 500 lost 1 percent to 7,341, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.7 percent to 24,328. Tech led the decline, with software stocks hit hard after OpenAI released new models, and investors stayed cautious ahead of Nvidia's earnings report after the bell. On the Fed, New York Fed President John Williams said the situation does not call for dramatic action, pushing back on the idea of a half point rate hike in December. He said inflation still has work to do to reach the Fed's 2 percent goal, pointing to tariffs, energy costs, and AI driven demand for chips. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem took a more hawkish line, saying several rate hikes are likely needed by spring. After the remarks, futures markets priced roughly a 98 percent chance of a quarter point hike at the December meeting. On the data side, October retail sales rose 0.2 percent, slightly better than expected, as shoppers kept spending ahead of the holidays. Next, Nvidia beat expectations in its first report since Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive last week. Revenue came in at about 115.8 billion dollars, more than double a year ago, and the company guided to about 130 billion dollars next quarter and announced a 150 billion dollar stock buyback. Shares rose in after hours trading. Next, Home Depot topped estimates with revenue of 43.4 billion dollars and its strongest comparable sales growth in four years, though it trimmed its operating margin outlook. The company also confirmed that its chief financial officer, Richard McPhail, takes over as chief executive on November 23. Next, Disney beat on both profit and revenue for its fiscal fourth quarter, helped by continued growth in its parks and streaming businesses. And finally, JPMorgan said chief financial officer Jeremy Barnum will step down next year, with Bregje de Best set to succeed him after the April earnings report. On the calendar today, Target, Lowe's, and TJX report earnings, with Palo Alto Networks also on deck. The Fed releases minutes from its October meeting at 2 p.m. Eastern, which is noon Mountain time. And Anthropic's initial public offering is expected to price today, ahead of a planned Nasdaq debut on Thursday. Here's your fun fact. In Estonia, drivers on the official winter ice roads across the frozen Baltic Sea are forbidden from wearing seatbelts, so they can escape quickly if the ice gives way. They are also told to avoid driving between about 25 and 40 kilometers per hour, because at those speeds a car can create a resonant wave under the ice that can crack it. Have a great day.
